live.name: GOLD HARVEST
live.headline: GOLD HARVEST: a threat actor tracked under several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists GOLD HARVEST under five other names and names three remote-access tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, tracks the actor as GOLD HARVEST.
The same record lists these aliases: Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
The record lists three tools: AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.headline: GOLD HARVEST (Scattered Spider): a social-engineering extortion crew that calls help desks
next.in_short: GOLD HARVEST, better known as Scattered Spider, is a financially motivated group. Vendors say it uses phone-based social engineering to take over accounts, steal data and sometimes deploy ransomware. Several links to other groups are…

sentences.t: The catalogue record for GOLD HARVEST, from Secureworks, lists these other names: Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
CrowdStrike calls Scattered Spider a prolific eCrime adversary that has run financially motivated activity since early 2022.
ReliaQuest describes it as a financially motivated cybercriminal gang associated with the hacking collective known as The Com.
Check Point, drawing on public intelligence, says the group is made up mainly of young people aged 19 to 22 from the US and UK.

EclecticIQ analysts assess that ShinyHunters is very likely relying on members of Scattered Spider and The Com for voice phishing. The same report says there is no direct relationship between the two groups.
Trustwave SpiderLabs reads the Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters brand, which borrows the Scattered Spider name, as a situational alliance and not a formal merger.
CrowdStrike says the group's early campaigns reportedly hit customer relationship management and business-process outsourcing firms, plus telecommunications and technology companies.

Halcyon says the group compromises call centres and other outsourcing providers to reach many clients at once. It says attacks on UK retail and US insurance likely began, at least in part, with such compromises.
ReliaQuest says 70% of the group's targets sit in technology, finance and retail trade.
Check Point says the group is now also targeting aviation. It ties this to media reports and advisories, including a July 2025 Qantas breach.
Mandiant says UNC3944 targets IT help desks to get around multifactor authentication.
Check Point lists phishing, SIM swapping, MFA fatigue, voice phishing, and tricking employees into installing remote access tools.
ReliaQuest says the group uses phishing frameworks such as Evilginx and short-lived typosquatted domains to bypass MFA.

Halcyon says the group has leaned on insider recruitment. It also cites driver abuse and evasion of endpoint security tools. It describes a data-first extortion model in which encryption is often an escalation step.
The catalogue lists the remote access tools AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein among the group's tools.
Sygnia names Scattered Spider among the groups that attack VMware ESXi virtualisation environments.

According to BleepingComputer's report, Scattered Spider breached MGM Resorts in September 2023. It got in by impersonating an employee, then encrypted over 100 VMware ESXi hypervisors with BlackCat ransomware.
ReliaQuest says a wave of attacks hit UK retailers, including Marks & Spencer, Co-op and Harrods, in May 2025. It says nothing definitive has tied those incidents to Scattered Spider.

In June 2025, Google's John Hultquist said Scattered Spider was targeting US insurers. The Aflac breach disclosed that month could not be attributed by a company spokesperson, though the report says it shows all the signs of the group.
Google tracks a Salesforce data-theft cluster, UNC6040, that starts with voice phishing. Google links its Okta phishing pages to actors associated with The Com or Scattered Spider tactics.
ReliaQuest sees plenty of circumstantial evidence of a deliberate partnership between ShinyHunters and Scattered Spider in the Salesforce attacks.
ReliaQuest says the group has struck alliances with ransomware operators ALPHV, RansomHub and DragonForce.

Rapid7 investigated an April 2026 intrusion that began with a Microsoft Teams message from a fake IT Support account. It says the approach mirrors tradecraft seen in Octo Tempest-style campaigns, and does not call it a confirmed link.
Verify any help-desk request to reset a password or an MFA method through a second, known channel before acting on it.
Treat unexpected IT or HR messages, including those in chat tools, as suspect until confirmed.
